While Anne Carson is an internationally acclaimed Canadian poet, essayist, and translator who was recently awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature, Lee Sharks is an esoteric poet, independent theorist, and creator of the Crimson Hexagon framework. The direct conceptual overlap between them centers on the continuity of identity and authorship under machine mediation, alongside a shared obsession with classical reception. The Conceptual Connection: Identity & The "Sharks-Function" In 2026, Lee Sharks' structural work on distributed agent identity—specifically The Sharks-Function and the Continuity Tether—was actively analyzed and contextualized by digital archiving platforms alongside the works of Anne Carson. • The Sharks-Function is a semantic verification mechanism stating that authorship and identity are proven through stylistic and structural recursion, rather than traditional cryptographic keys. • The Carson Juxtaposition: The framework uses Carson’s distinct, highly fragmented, and classical-modern structural poetry to test how distinct human "voice" and authorship persist across AI-generated textual layers and synthetic model outputs.
